title: Relativistic Persistence
relevance: Primary treatment of persistence in relativistic spacetime; bears on the paper's pointy versus bow-tie realm choice and on the word 'persistence' in Prop. sp
limits: Partial read as listed; the 'relativity rules out presentism' claim is the authors' assumption, not a settled result (Dorato, Monton are cited in the repository's bibliography as dissenters)
version: PhilSci-Archive 2845 preprint, 25 July 2006 (44 pp.); published Philosophical Perspectives 20 (2006) 157-198, DOI 10.1111/j.1520-8583.2006.00106.x (Crossref metadata only)
locators: Sec. 1; Sec. 2 (taking relativity seriously; 2.1 relativistic perdurance, critique of frame-relativized definitions incl. Sider 2001 p. 59); Sec. 3 (Balashov coexistence argument, opening and notes); Sec. 4 (Hales-Johnson argument, premises 1-7 reproduced and answered); Sec. 5 (Gilmore's four principles and the Every C-Slice Principle, opening); Sec. 6 (end: Balashov on explanatory deficiency)
assumptions: Eternalism and a tenseless theory of time; relativity rules out non-eternalism and tensed theories; persistence doctrines must be stated with spacetime regions, not times
conclusion: Authors' claims: the recent arguments against relativistic endurantism (Balashov, Hales-Johnson) fail; the defensible relativistic endurantism is multilocation in achronal slices (Every Slice Principle, maximal achronal regions); frame-relativizing Sider's definitions is wrong-headed
proof_status: Read from a pdf-to-text extraction with lost spacing; no independent check of the arguments
open_questions: Section 2.2 (preferred form of relativistic endurance), the rest of Sec. 3, the body of Sec. 4 and Sec. 5, and Sec. 7 not fully read; whether Every Slice survives curved, non-globally-hyperbolic spacetimes

title: Where in the Relativistic World Are We?
relevance: Gives the Location Question that the paper's realm-structure choice parallels
limits: Preprint, about half read via pdf extraction; not the published version
version: PhilSci-Archive 2979 preprint (2006); published Philosophical Perspectives 20 (2006) 199-236, DOI 10.1111/j.1520-8583.2006.00107.x (as given in Gibson-Pooley references)
locators: Sec. 0-1 (exact occupation, five conditions); Sec. 2 (D1-D5: path, achronal, persist, worm, saint); Sec. 3 (segmented/non-segmented cross-cut); Sec. 4 opening (Location Question, Path and Absolute Slice Principles) and 4.1 (Every Slice, first two considerations and replies; D6 maximal achronal region)
assumptions: B-theoretic spacetime substantivalism; exact occupation primitive allowing multilocation
conclusion: Author's claim: worm theory and saint (endurance-type) theory differ about which regions an object exactly occupies; for saints in relativistic spacetime no location principle is obviously right; he raises problems for the Rest Frame, Top Down, Bottom Up and Every Slice principles (the later critiques were read only via Gibson-Pooley)
proof_status: Definitions and informal argument read; nothing to reproduce
open_questions: Read only to the end of Sec. 4.1's first part; remaining objections to Every Slice and the rest of the paper not read

title: Persistence and Multilocation in Spacetime
relevance: Source for the three-way definitions used in READING.md sec. 1
limits: Which publication this PDF is cannot be fixed from the file; read as an author's text
version: Author-hosted PDF headed 'Chapter 4' (23 pp.); the OUP book Persistence and Spacetime (2010) has a chapter 'Persistence, Location, and Multilocation in Spacetime', DOI 10.1093/acprof:oso/9780199579921.003.0002 (Crossref metadata); not verified to be the same text
locators: Abstract and Sec. 1-2 (generic spacetime framework, D1 achronal, D3 LOCATED via non-modal counterparts, D4-D5 path and persists); D6-D10 (achronal and diachronic parts); D11-D13 (endures, perdures, exdures)
assumptions: Eternalist spacetime; exact location primitive; counterparts count as improper counterparts of themselves
conclusion: Author's claim: endurance, perdurance and exdurance can be stated in a common spacetime framework; exdurance counts as persistence on the broad notion of LOCATION
proof_status: Definitions read by text search and sections 1-2; no independent check
open_questions: Applications to Galilean and Minkowski spacetime and the closing objection not read

title: Four-Dimensionalism
relevance: Primary source for argument B and for the independence-of-presentism footnote
limits: Read from a pdf extraction in which about two thirds of the paper was skimmed
version: Author PDF of Philosophical Review 106 (1997) 197-231, DOI 10.2307/2998357 (from PhilPapers record, not checked in Crossref)
locators: Sec. 1-2 (formulating four-dimensionalism by existence-at and parthood-at; 'wholly present' definitions WP and WP2-WP7; n. 9 and n. 12 on presentism); Sec. 3 (argument from vagueness, P1'-P3', U, Thesis of Temporal Locality)
assumptions: Vagueness never arises from logic; existence-at distinguished from quantification; non-presentist framework adopted for convenience
conclusion: Author's claims: four-dimensionalism is formulable neutrally, three-dimensionalism is hard to formulate; every assignment of objects to times has a minimal diachronic fusion, hence temporal parts exist; presentism is independent of four-dimensionalism (cited from Sider 1996b)
proof_status: Argument sketch and proof footnote read; not re-derived
open_questions: Sec. 4 onward and the replies to objections not read; Sider 2001 book chapter not accessed
